questions.q: How many boxes are kept between box N and box O?
questions.solution: The final arrangement from top to bottom is: N, L, K, P, I, J, O, M. Box N is at the top and box O is seventh, so boxes L, K, P, I and J - five boxes - lie between them, which is more than four. **Answer: More than four**
questions.shortcut: Fix M at the bottom via the K-M count, then cascade.
questions.passage: Directions (Q.1-4): Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Eight boxes - I, J, K, L, M, N, O and P - are kept one above another in a single stack but not necessarily in the same order. Four boxes are kept between box K and box M. Box N is kept two boxes above box K. Two boxes are kept between box N and box P. Box P and box I are kept adjacent to each other. Box J is kept immediately above box O. As many boxes are kept below box O as above box L.

questions.q: If all the boxes are arranged in alphabetical order from top to bottom, then how many boxes remain unchanged in their position?
questions.solution: The final stack is N, L, K, P, I, J, O, M. In alphabetical order (I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P), position 3 should hold K and position 7 should hold O - exactly the boxes already there. Every other position changes, so two boxes remain unchanged. **Answer: Two**

questions.q: Which among the following boxes is/are kept above box P?
options: Both box K and box N
questions.solution: In the stack N, L, K, P, I, J, O, M, box P is fourth. The boxes above it are N, L and K. Among the options, both box K and box N are above P, while M and J are below it. **Answer: Both box K and box N**

questions.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are not true? I. No box is kept below box M. II. Box I is kept below box O. III. An even number of boxes are kept below box L.
questions.solution: In the stack N, L, K, P, I, J, O, M: statement I is true because M is at the bottom. Statement II is false because I (fifth) is above O (seventh). Statement III is true because six boxes lie below L, and six is even. Hence only statement II is not true. **Answer: Only II**

questions.q: What is the code for the words "Justice prevail"?
questions.solution: Comparing sentences 3 and 4, 'justice' is the only common word and 'hj' is the only common code, so justice = hj. In sentence 4 the remaining codes xt and bo belong to 'must' and 'prevail' in an unknown order, so the code of 'prevail' cannot be fixed. Hence the code for 'justice prevail' cannot be determined. **Answer: Can’t be determined**
questions.passage: Directions (Q.5-9): Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. In a certain code language: "Justice delayed is denied" is coded as "bv hj kr jh". "Police denied public safety" is coded as "jh rt nh tf". "Delayed trial denied justice" is coded as "hj jh jc bv". "Public justice must prevail" is coded as "hj xt bo nh".

questions.q: Which among the following word pairs is coded as "kr nh"?
questions.solution: 'kr' appears only in sentence 1, whose leftover word is 'is', so kr = is. 'nh' is common to sentences 2 and 4, whose only common word is 'public', so nh = public. Hence 'kr nh' stands for 'is public'. **Answer: Is public**

questions.q: If "Delayed prevail order" is coded as "bv bo ot", then what is the code for "Must order"?
questions.solution: From this extra clue, 'order' = ot (a new code), and comparing with sentence 4 where justice = hj and public = nh, 'prevail' must be bo, leaving 'must' = xt. Therefore 'must order' = xt ot, i.e. 'ot xt'. **Answer: ot xt**

questions.q: Which among the following statements is/are not correct? I. Public is coded as "nh". II. Police can be coded as "rt". III. Delayed trial is coded as "bv xt".
questions.solution: Statement I is correct: nh = public. Statement II is correct: 'police' appears only in sentence 2, where the leftover codes rt and tf are shared with 'safety', so police can be rt. Statement III is incorrect: delayed = bv and trial = jc (leftover of sentence 3), so 'delayed trial' = bv jc, not bv xt. Only statement III is not correct. **Answer: Only III**

questions.q: What is the code of the word "trial"?
questions.solution: In sentence 3, 'delayed', 'denied' and 'justice' map to bv, jh and hj respectively (delayed = bv from sentences 1 and 3, denied = jh, justice = hj). The remaining word 'trial' takes the remaining code 'jc'. **Answer: jc**

questions.q: Who among the following lives in Flat A of the 3rd floor?
questions.solution: The final arrangement is: Floor 4 - E (flat-A), D (flat-B); Floor 3 - A (flat-A), G (flat-B); Floor 2 - C (flat-A), B (flat-B); Floor 1 - H (flat-A), F (flat-B). G is in flat-B, E (flat-A) is on even floor 4 above G, and the flat-A column from bottom is H, C, A, E. So flat-A of the 3rd floor is A. **Answer: A**
questions.passage: Directions (Q.10-14): Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. There are eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H living in a building (but not necessarily in the same order) having four floors such that the ground floor is numbered as 1 and the floor just above it is numbered as 2, and so on till the topmost floor is numbered as 4. Each floor consists of two types of flats, i.e., flat-A and flat-B. Flat-A of floor 2 is immediately above flat-A of floor 1 and immediately below flat-A of floor 3, and in the same way flat-B of floor 2 is immediately above flat-B of floor 1 and immediately below flat-B of floor 3, and so on. Also, flat-A is to the west of flat-B. G lives in flat-B. H lives to the west of F. H and A live in the same type of flat. A lives above H. C and B live on the same floor. B lives below the floor of D and both live in the same type of flat. E lives above G. E and G do not live in the same type of flat. There is one floor gap between G's floor and F's floor. E lives on an even-numbered floor.

questions.q: Who lives immediately above G in the same type of flat as G lives?
questions.solution: G lives in flat-B of the 3rd floor. In the same flat type (flat-B), the person immediately above is on the 4th floor flat-B, which is D. **Answer: D**

questions.q: Who among the following lives in Flat A of the 2nd floor?
questions.solution: The flat-A column from floor 1 to 4 is H, C, A, E. Hence flat-A of the 2nd floor is occupied by C. **Answer: C**

questions.q: Who lives exactly between G and F in the same type of flat?
questions.solution: G (flat-B, 3rd floor) and F (flat-B, 1st floor) have exactly one floor - the 2nd - between them. The flat-B occupant of the 2nd floor is B. **Answer: B**

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
options: D lives on a floor below F in the same type of flat
A lives on a floor above D
E and H live on consecutive floors
B and F live in same type of flat
questions.solution: Checking each option against the final arrangement: D (4th, flat-B) is above F, not below; A (3rd) is below D (4th); E is on floor 4 and H on floor 1, not consecutive; D (flat-B, east) is not west of E (flat-A, west). But B and F both live in flat-B (floors 2 and 1), so the last statement is true. **Answer: B and F live in same type of flat**

questions.q: If in the given series each number is increased by 1, how many numbers will be odd?
questions.solution: Adding 1 to each number: 414, 877, 264, 515, 892. Of these, 877 and 515 are odd, so exactly two numbers become odd. **Answer: Two**
questions.shortcut: Even + 1 = odd: count original even numbers.
questions.passage: Directions (Q.15-19): Read the given series of five 3-digit numbers carefully and answer the questions based on it: 413  876  263  514  891

questions.q: If the digits of each number are arranged in ascending order, which number becomes the smallest?
questions.solution: Rearranging digits of each number in ascending order: 413 -> 134, 876 -> 678, 263 -> 236, 514 -> 145, 891 -> 189. The smallest resulting number is 134, which comes from 413. **Answer: 413**

questions.q: What is the product of the first digit of the third number from the left and the last digit of the second number from the right?
questions.solution: The third number from the left is 263, whose first digit is 2. The second number from the right is 514, whose last digit is 4. Product = 2 x 4 = 8. **Answer: 8**

questions.q: If the even digits of each number are removed, which number will be the highest?
questions.solution: Removing even digits: 413 -> 13, 876 -> 7, 263 -> 3, 514 -> 51, 891 -> 91. The highest remaining number is 91, formed from 891. **Answer: 891**

questions.q: What is the sum of the highest digit of the third number from the left end and the second highest digit of the fourth number from the right end in the series?
questions.solution: The third number from the left is 263; its highest digit is 6. The fourth number from the right end is 876; its digits in decreasing order are 8, 7, 6, so the second highest is 7. Sum = 6 + 7 = 13. **Answer: 13**

questions.q: How many females are in the family?
questions.solution: The family tree: N (male) and J (female) have son K and daughter M (M must be K's sister because D, M's husband, is the son-in-law of K's mother, and 'their daughter-in-law is not M' rules M out as J's daughter-in-law). K is married to U and their child is H; M is married to D and their child is B. A is U's unmarried sister. K, H and B must all be male, otherwise the female count would exceed four. Females: A, U, M, J - four in total. **Answer: Four**
questions.passage: Directions (Q.20-22): Read the given information carefully and answer the related questions. A is the unmarried sister of U, who is the spouse of K. D is the son-in-law of K's mother. M is the parent of B, who is the child of D. N is the grandfather of B and H. J is the spouse of N but their daughter-in-law is not M. J's son has a child. K, H and B are of the same gender.

questions.q: What is the relation of U's child with respect to B?
questions.solution: U's child is H (child of K and U). B is the child of M and D. K and M are siblings (children of N and J), so their children H and B are first cousins. **Answer: Cousin**

questions.q: Who among the following is the child of K?
questions.solution: N is the grandfather of both B and H. B is already the child of M and D, so H must be the grandchild through N's other child K, i.e. H is the child of K and U. **Answer: H**

questions.q: How many pairs of letters are there in the word "BUTTERFLY" in both forward and backward directions, each of which has as many letters between them in the word as in the English alphabetical series?
questions.solution: Number the letters: B(1) U(2) T(3) T(4) E(5) R(6) F(7) L(8) Y(9). Checking pairs, the valid ones are U-T (one letter between in the word; U to T is also one step in the alphabet), T-R (positions 4 and 6, one letter between; T to R is two alphabet steps with one letter between) and T-Y (positions 4 and 9, four letters between; T to Y has four letters between in the alphabet). That gives three such pairs. **Answer: Three**
questions.shortcut: For a pair, |gap in word| must equal |gap in alphabet|.

questions.q: Who among the following was born in June?
questions.solution: The final arrangement is: January - F, March - G, April - D, June - E, July - B, August - C, November - H, December - A. H must be in a 30-day month after April (June or November); the count conditions force November for H, December for A, and then June falls to E. **Answer: E**
questions.passage: Directions (Q.24-28): Read the given information carefully and answer the questions that follow. Eight persons - A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H - were born on the same date but in different months of the same year, namely January, March, April, June, July, August, November and December (not necessarily in the same order). H was born in the month having an even number of days after the month of April. Three persons were born between H and D. There was a gap of three months between the birth months of D and C. A was born after C. As many persons were born before A as after F. Two persons were born between F and E. B was born after E.

questions.q: Four of the following five are alike in a certain manner and hence form a group. Which one does not belong to that group?
questions.solution: From the arrangement: C was born in August (31 days), F in January (31 days), A in December (31 days) and G in March (31 days), while D was born in April, a 30-day month. So D is the odd one out. **Answer: D**

questions.q: G was born in which of the following months?
questions.solution: A is born after C, with as many persons before A as after F, which forces A to December and F to January. Two persons between F and E put E in June, and the remaining slots give G the month of March. **Answer: March**

questions.q: How many persons were born between F and H?
questions.solution: F was born in January (position 1) and H in November (position 7) of the eight-month sequence. The persons between them occupy March, April, June, July and August - five persons. **Answer: Five**

questions.q: If all the persons are arranged in alphabetical order from the first month to the last month, then how many persons will remain at the same position?
questions.solution: Chronological order of persons is F, G, D, E, B, C, H, A. Arranged alphabetically the sequence would need to be A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H in months January through December. Comparing: A is in December (not January), B in July (not March), C in August (not April), D in April (not June), E in June (not July), F in January (not August), G in March (not November), H in November (not December). Not a single person keeps the same month, so none remain in position. **Answer: None**

questions.q: Statements: Only a few magnet is pole. All magnet is material. Some material is metal. Conclusions: I. All material being pole is a possibility. II. Some magnet is not pole. In the question, some statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically does not follow from the given statements.
options: If either conclusion I or II follows
If neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution: 'Only a few magnet is pole' means some magnets are poles and some magnets are definitely not poles. So conclusion II ('Some magnet is not pole') definitely follows. Since every magnet is material, the non-pole magnets are material that is not pole, making it impossible for all material to be pole - conclusion I does not follow. As the question asks which conclusion does NOT follow, only conclusion I qualifies. **Answer: If only conclusion I follows**

questions.q: Statements: All doors are tables. Some tables are not wooden. Only wooden is plastic. Conclusions: I. All plastic can never be doors. II. Some wooden are not tables. In the question, two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to assume all the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the information given in the statements.
options: If either conclusion I or II follows
If neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution: 'Only wooden is plastic' means every plastic thing is wooden, but a plastic item can still be a door, because doors are tables and a table may be wooden - so it is possible for plastic to be doors, and conclusion I does not follow. Conclusion II claims some wooden things are not tables, but 'some tables are not wooden' gives no information forcing any wooden item outside the tables, so II also does not follow. Neither conclusion follows. **Answer: If neither conclusion I nor II follows**

questions.q: Statements: Only a few Notes are Important. All Notes are Papers. No Papers are File. Conclusions: I. Some notes are not file. II. No important are file. In the question, two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to assume all the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the information given in the statements.
options: If either conclusion I or II follows
If neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution: 'Only a few Notes are Important' guarantees at least some notes exist. All notes are papers, and no paper is a file, so no note is a file - conclusion I ('Some notes are not file') follows. For conclusion II, only a part of the notes is important; important things outside the notes are unconstrained and could well be files, so 'No important are file' does not follow. Only conclusion I follows. **Answer: If only conclusion I follows**

questions.q: Who among the following is the third shortest person?
questions.solution: The height order from tallest to shortest is: S, P, R (168 cm), T, V, Q, W (152 cm), U. The third shortest is the person at position 6, which is Q. **Answer: Q**
questions.passage: Directions (Q.32-35): Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Eight persons - P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W - have different heights (not necessarily in the same order). No two persons have the same height. R is taller than V but shorter than S. T is taller than Q. Only three persons are shorter than V. Q is three persons shorter than R. The sum of the heights of R and W is 320 cm. T is shorter than R but taller than W. As many persons are taller than W as shorter than P. S is not shorter than P. The height of R is 168 cm.

questions.q: How many persons are taller than P?
questions.solution: In the final order S, P, R, T, V, Q, W, U, only S stands above P. So exactly one person is taller than P. **Answer: One**

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
options: P is not taller than V.
Exactly two persons are taller than P.
questions.solution: Checking each option: P is taller than V, so (a) is false; exactly one person (S) is taller than P, so (c) is false; Q is shorter than R, so (d) is false; W is the second shortest, so (e) is false. U is the shortest person, so statement (b) is true. **Answer: U is the shortest person.**

questions.q: What is the possible height of T?
questions.solution: R is 168 cm, so W = 320 - 168 = 152 cm. T sits between R and W in height (shorter than R, taller than W), so T's height lies strictly between 152 cm and 168 cm. Among the options, only 160 cm falls in that range. **Answer: 160cm**
questions.shortcut: R + W = 320 fixes W = 152; T is bracketed between 152 and 168.
